channel.title: vocab.design
channel.description: A linked visual dictionary of design and UI vocabulary: new entries as they are published.

item.title: Anti-pattern
item.description: A solution reached for again and again for a familiar problem, which fails at the thing it was reached for and often leaves the situation worse than doing nothing.

item.title: Contribution graph
item.description: A year of days as a grid of week columns, each cell shaded by how much happened that day, so a habit reads as a pattern instead of a number.

item.title: Easter egg
item.description: A reward hidden behind an action nobody was told about, put there to be found rather than to be used.

item.title: Error page
item.description: The whole screen a site serves instead of the page that was asked for: what happened, in the reader's words, and the shortest way back to something that works.

item.title: Fake door
item.description: A control that looks shipped and leads nowhere, put in the interface on purpose to count how many people want the feature behind it.

item.title: Fine print
item.description: Qualifying text set small and set last, carrying the conditions that the larger claim above it leaves out.

item.title: Microcopy
item.description: An interface's smallest strings: the verb on the button, the line under the field, the sentence when it fails. Short enough to be read every time.

item.title: Mockup
item.description: A screen shown as it will look rather than as it will work: colour, type and real copy all settled, and nothing in it clickable.

item.title: Prototype
item.description: A design wired up just enough to be tried: screens linked so that a tap goes somewhere, with nothing real behind the links.

item.title: Wireframe
item.description: A screen drawn as structure only: blocks where the content goes, a crossed box for an image, ruled lines for text, with no colour or type decided yet.

item.title: Additive colour
item.description: Colour made by adding light, where red, green and blue at full strength give white, which is why a screen is at its brightest when it is showing all three.

item.title: Agenda view
item.description: The same events as a chronological list grouped by day, so the next thing is at the top instead of somewhere inside a grid.

item.title: Autoplay
item.description: Playback that starts with no gesture from the reader, which browsers now allow only while the sound is off, so autoplay in practice means a silent moving picture.

item.title: Blame view
item.description: Each line of a file labelled with the change that last touched it, so the file answers who and when rather than what it says.

item.title: Bulletproof button
item.description: A mail button built to survive a renderer that drops CSS: the fill carried by a cell or box behind the link rather than by a background the client can refuse.

item.title: Color coding
item.description: Giving each category its own colour so the eye can group and find by hue, which holds only while the set stays small and one colour means one thing everywhere.

item.title: Concentric corner radius
item.description: Sizing a nested shape's corners so its curve shares a centre with the one outside it, the inner radius being the outer radius less the padding between them.

item.title: Conversational interface
item.description: An interface operated in turns of language rather than by controls, where the transcript is the state and the only visible affordance is a box to type in.

item.title: Corner radius
item.description: How far a shape's corners are rounded off, measured as the radius of the circle that replaces the square angle, and the one number that decides how soft a UI reads.

item.title: Dark mode email
item.description: Designing a mail for clients that will invert its palette without asking, where a near-black behaves better than black and a logo needs a ground it survives on.

item.title: Diff viewer
item.description: The view that puts two versions of a text against each other, side by side or interleaved, marking every line added, removed or changed and aligning what did not.

item.title: Digital rain
item.description: Columns of glyphs falling and trailing away, green on black, the Matrix screen quoted so often that it now reads as shorthand for a computer thinking.

item.title: Double opt-in
item.description: Asking a new subscriber to confirm from the address they typed, so a list holds only addresses whose owner agreed and a typo never becomes a stranger's mail.

item.title: Drag to create
item.description: Making a new object by dragging out its extent rather than pressing Add: an event drawn across two hours, a frame drawn on a canvas, a range drawn on a chart.

item.title: Edge routing
item.description: How a connector gets from one node to another: a bezier sweep, a right-angled staircase, or a straight line, picked so the crossings stay readable.

item.title: Elevation
item.description: How high a surface sits above the one behind it, expressed as a shadow, a tint, or both, and held to a few named steps so that height means something.

item.title: Flame graph
item.description: Stacked bars where width is time spent and depth is call nesting, so the widest plateau rather than the tallest tower is the thing worth fixing.

item.title: Flowchart
item.description: A diagram of steps in boxes joined by arrows, read rather than operated, and now more often generated from a few lines of text than drawn by hand.

item.title: Fluid hybrid
item.description: A mail layout that reflows with no media query at all: percentage widths held in by max-width, with fixed-width ghost tables that only Outlook can see.

item.title: Gantt chart
item.description: One row per task with a bar along a time axis, the bar showing when the work runs and lines between bars showing what waits for what.

item.title: Graph layout
item.description: Placing the nodes of a wired diagram by algorithm rather than by hand: layered for a flow, radial for a hub, force-directed for a mesh that has no direction.

item.title: Hidden gesture
item.description: An action reachable only by an input the reader has to guess: a swipe, a long press, a two-finger tap, with nothing on screen saying it is there.

item.title: Interest invoker
item.description: A link or button that shows more when a reader shows interest in it, by hovering, focusing or long pressing, with no click and no script deciding what interest means.

item.title: Invoker command
item.description: A button that names the element it acts on and what to do to it, in markup, so opening a dialog or toggling a popover needs no script at all.

item.title: Node graph
item.description: A canvas of boxes wired to each other by lines, where each box does one job and the wiring between them is the thing being built, rearranged by dragging.

item.title: Node port
item.description: The typed stub on a node where a wire may land, coloured or shaped by what it accepts, so a connection that would make no sense refuses to complete.

item.title: Operational transparency
item.description: Showing the work as it happens, the kitchen made visible, so a wait is understood rather than merely endured and the result is trusted more for having been watched.

item.title: Oversized typography
item.description: Type set far past reading size so the words carry the layout, the headline doing the work a photograph would otherwise be hired for.

item.title: Preview text
item.description: The line an inbox prints under a subject, written as hidden text at the top of the mail so the client shows those words instead of scraping whatever body copy comes first.

item.title: Print stylesheet
item.description: The rules that decide what a page becomes on paper: navigation dropped, link targets spelled out, backgrounds abandoned, and the content given page margins.

item.title: Recurring event
item.description: An event stored once as a rule instead of as copies, so every second Tuesday can be edited, skipped for one week, or ended, without touching the rest.

item.title: Scheduler
item.description: A grid of days crossed with hours where each event is a block in its own slot, so a week's free time is visible and an event is moved by dragging it.

item.title: Sender name
item.description: The name a mail appears to come from, chosen rather than inherited, because a reader scanning an inbox decides on it before reading a word of the subject.

item.title: Styled alt text
item.description: Alt text given size, colour and weight so a mail whose images are blocked still reads as something designed instead of as a column of grey stubs.

item.title: Subject line
item.description: The one line a mail is opened or ignored on, written to survive a list that truncates it and shows it wedged between the sender and the preview text.

item.title: Subtractive colour
item.description: Colour made by taking light away, where inks stack towards black and every added layer can only darken, which is why a screen blue cannot be printed.

item.title: Syntax highlighting
item.description: Colouring code by what each token is, keyword or string or comment or name, so the structure and the typo are visible before a line has actually been read.

item.title: Table-based layout
item.description: Laying a page out in nested tables because the renderer has no box model worth trusting, which is how mail is still built and how the web was built before CSS.

item.title: Three-way merge
item.description: Three versions on screen at once, mine, theirs, and the ancestor they both came from, with the result edited underneath so a conflict is decided rather than guessed.

item.title: Time zone display
item.description: Whose clock a time is shown on, the reader's or the event's, and saying which, because a time with no zone beside it is a meeting somebody is going to miss.

item.title: Top shelf
item.description: The band across the top of a television home screen that the focused app fills with its own content, so an app advertises itself before anyone opens it.

item.title: Trace viewer
item.description: The view that lays a request's spans on one time axis, each nested under the span that called it, so the bar that is too long or starts too late is the finding.

item.title: Transactional email
item.description: Mail sent because one person did one thing, a receipt or a reset, which is why it may carry no marketing and why its design is a record rather than a pitch.

item.title: Unsubscribe link
item.description: The way out of a mailing list, which the law and the mail clients now both insist is one click, and whose difficulty is the honest measure of a sender.

item.title: Autofill
item.description: The browser filling a form from values it has already saved, on its own or from a dropdown of the reader's own profile, so a field arrives answered.

item.title: Hydration
item.description: The pass where script attaches behaviour to server-rendered HTML, turning a page that is already painted and readable into one that answers input.

item.title: Labor illusion
item.description: Showing the work a system is doing, or stretching it, so the answer feels earned: the search that lists the sites it is checking instead of answering at once.

item.title: Overloaded command
item.description: One command word or icon wired to different outcomes depending on where it sits, so having used it once teaches the reader nothing about the next one.

item.title: Speculative loading
item.description: Fetching, or fully rendering, a page before the reader asks for it, on a guess about where they go next, so the navigation is already done when the click lands.

item.title: 10-foot UI
item.description: The register for screens read from a couch: focus-driven navigation with a remote, oversized type and cards, horizontal rails, and safe margins for TV overscan.

item.title: 12 column grid
item.description: The web's default column count, chosen because twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.

item.title: 3D tilt
item.description: Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.

item.title: 60-30-10 rule
item.description: A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.

item.title: 8 point grid
item.description: A spacing convention where every size and gap is a multiple of eight, so values stay whole numbers at every common screen density.

item.title: Abbreviation
item.description: A shortened form of a word or phrase, from Dr. to NASA, with its own typographic conventions and an expansion assistive tech can speak.

item.title: Accent color
item.description: The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.

item.title: Access key
item.description: A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.

item.title: Accessibility annotation
item.description: Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.

item.title: Accessibility grouping
item.description: Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.

item.title: Accessibility overlay
item.description: A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.

item.title: Accessibility trait
item.description: The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.

item.title: Accessibility tree
item.description: The parallel tree a browser derives from the DOM, holding the role, name, state, and value that assistive technology actually reads.

item.title: Accessible authentication
item.description: A sign-in route that never requires a cognitive function test such as recalling a password or solving a puzzle without offering an alternative.

item.title: Accessible description
item.description: Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.

item.title: Accessible name
item.description: The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.

item.title: Accordion
item.description: A stack of headers, each expanding to reveal its own section of content.

item.title: Achievement badge
item.description: A collectible marker awarded for a milestone and displayed on a profile, often shown greyed out before it is earned so the set is visible.

item.title: Acid graphics
item.description: A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated colour on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.

item.title: Action list
item.description: A vertical list of commands with icons, descriptions and dividers, the shared body used inside menus, panels and side sheets.

item.title: Action sheet
item.description: A modal list of choices that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen in response to something you just did, with cancel at the end.

item.title: Active descendant
item.description: A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.

item.title: Activity feed
item.description: A reverse chronological list of things that happened, each entry naming an actor, a verb, and an object, grouped when many are alike.

item.title: Adaptive layout
item.description: A layout that switches between a few discrete arrangements chosen per size class, rather than flowing continuously as the window changes.

item.title: Additive animation
item.description: Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.

item.title: Address autocomplete
item.description: Replacing a set of address fields with one lookup that suggests full addresses after a few characters and fills the rest on selection.

item.title: Affordance
item.description: What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.

item.title: Afrofuturism
item.description: A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.

item.title: Alert dialog
item.description: A dialog that interrupts the flow to demand acknowledgement or confirmation of a consequential action before anything else can continue.

item.title: All caps
item.description: Text set entirely in capitals, which reads slower than mixed case because the word's outline shape disappears.

item.title: Alpha channel
item.description: The transparency component carried inside a colour value itself, which lets a border or fill blend with whatever surface it lands on instead of assuming one.

item.title: Alpha compositing
item.description: The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.

item.title: Alt text
item.description: The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.

item.title: Analogous colors
item.description: A palette built from hues that neighbour each other on the wheel, giving a calm scheme with no colour fighting another for attention.

item.title: Anchor positioning
item.description: A CSS mechanism that tethers one element to another, sizing and placing it against its anchor and trying fallback positions when the default one would overflow.

item.title: Anti-design
item.description: A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.

item.title: Anticipation
item.description: A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.

item.title: APCA
item.description: A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.

item.title: Aperture
item.description: The partly enclosed opening in a letter, such as the gap where the two terminals of a c stop or the mouth at the bottom of an e.

item.title: App bar
item.description: The persistent bar across the top of an application carrying its title, navigation, and primary actions.

item.title: App shell
item.description: The persistent frame of an application, its header, navigation and footer, that stays put while only the content region swaps as you move around.
